summary.text: The basis of the Moscow school of painting was the synthesis of local traditions with Byzantine and South Slavic art. … The flourishing of the Moscow school in the late 14th and early 15th centuries is associated with Theophanes the Greek, Andrei Rublev and Daniel Chorny.
For a whole century Rublev’s influence determined the destiny of Russian art; but at the end of the 15th century the style which he originated lost its classic severity and tended to mere elegance.

source.author: Victoria and Albert Museum
